close_reason: Applied option 1 from the bead — mechanical wording tightening. Added a clarifying sentence to the SharingBackend stability carve-out noting that (a) the trait currently has no default-method bodies, (b) every present method materially affects wire-protocol correctness and cannot be no-op-defaulted without silently breaking the response, and (c) the carve-out applies only to future additions that can be given a sensible default (capability probes, audit hooks), with a clean SemVer-breaking minor-release bump as the transition path for methods that cannot. This avoids the workspace-architectural decision between options 2 (ship supports_type as default) and 3 (deprecated-trait + new-trait pattern), which the bead itself acknowledges is premature before the first real transition. Propagation to canonical mail-server's stability block: it does not yet carry the stability block at all (this sharing-server crate is the prototype), so propagation is not relevant in this pass. clippy clean, fmt clean. Doc warnings unchanged.
description:
**Location**: `crate-jmap-sharing-server/src/lib.rs:34-38`.

**The promise**:

> - **[\`SharingBackend\`] trait** (\`crate::backend\`): methods MAY be added
>   in a minor release. Adding a required method is a breaking change for
>   downstream impls; the workspace will signal such changes via
>   CHANGELOG entries and (where practical) \`#[deprecated]\` warnings or
>   default-method bodies during a transition release.

**Why this is a contract concern**: the promised mitigation —
default-method bodies during a transition release — has zero
precedent in the current trait shape. Reading `backend.rs:61-234`:

```
fn create_object<O: SetObject + Send + Sync>(...) -> impl Future<...> + Send;
fn update_object<O: SetObject + Send + Sync>(...) -> impl Future<...> + Send;
fn destroy_object<O: SetObject + Send + Sync>(...) -> impl Future<...> + Send;
fn supports_type<O: JmapObject>(&self) -> bool;
```

Every method is required. There is no `supports_type` default body
(it's required, and the in-tree impls all just return `true`). There
is no `default` keyword anywhere in the trait. The promise made in
lib.rs:34-38 is the workspace's GENERAL pre-1.0 stability discipline,
but this specific trait gives a downstream implementor no example to
follow if a new method is added "with a default body during a
transition release".

**Three plausible refinements**:

1. **Tighten the promise to match reality**: change "or default-method
   bodies" to "or default-method bodies where the new method can be
   given a sensible no-op default". Acknowledges that the trait is
   currently shaped such that every method materially affects
   correctness (no method can be no-op-defaulted without silently
   breaking the wire protocol).

2. **Demonstrate the discipline now**: ship `supports_type` with a
   default body `{ true }` so the trait carries one example of the
   pattern. This would let a downstream impl that doesn't care omit
   the method. (Note: both in-tree impls already return `true`
   unconditionally — bd:JMAP-3t94.20 closed the doc gap on this.)

3. **Reframe the carve-out**: instead of "default-method bodies",
   commit to a "deprecated-trait + new-trait" transition pattern
   (e.g. `SharingBackendV2: SharingBackend` with new methods, then
   blanket impl `V2` for any `Backend` that doesn't override).
   Heavier but more honest.

**Severity**: P3, not P0/P1. This is not a wire-protocol bug or a
silent breakage. It is a documented carve-out the codebase has not
yet exercised. The risk is asymmetric — a downstream implementor
reads the promise, infers the maintainer plans to use default-method
bodies, and writes their own trait around that expectation. When the
first SemVer transition happens and the carve-out turns out to be a
hard break, the implementor's downstream consumers carry the cost.

**Workspace-wide shape**: every `*-server` crate has a similar
stability statement (bd:JMAP-3t94.23 added the policy block here;
the canonical mail-server has the same one). A workspace-wide
tightening pass on the wording would resolve the same gap in 7
other crates.

**Confidence**: this is a real engineering concern but it is low-grade
relative to the wire-protocol findings already filed under this epic.
Reasonable maintainers could decline this finding on the grounds that
"the workspace has not yet had a real opportunity to demonstrate
either the default-method pattern OR the deprecated-trait pattern,
and tightening the wording before the first transition is premature".
That counterargument is honored — file with P3 and decide on the
canonical mail-server.
title: Pre-1.0 stability promise of 'deprecated warnings or default-method bodies during transition' has zero precedent — SharingBackend has no default methods
